warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of a phishing/fraud scam: it asks for payment of a utility advance ('Abschlag') to a newly-announced IBAN whose account holder is 'Global Energy Payments s.r.o.', not the utility itself.
The stated IBAN (DE61 2004 1111 0512 3456 78) fails the standard IBAN checksum validation, meaning it is not a properly formed/genuine account number.
The letter uses classic pressure tactics: an extremely short payment deadline and a threat of immediate, unannounced service disconnection.
It instructs the recipient not to reply in writing and to call only a mobile phone number instead of the utility's normal channels, which is a common scam pattern.
The sender's email domain ('kundenservice-mail.example') does not look like an official Stadtwerke Musterstadt domain.
Do not transfer any money based on this letter; contact Stadtwerke Musterstadt directly using contact details from a previous genuine bill or their official website to verify.
data.title: Suspicious letter: alleged Stadtwerke bank-account change demanding urgent payment
data.summary: A letter claiming to be from Stadtwerke Musterstadt (customer number 300 441 872) states its bank details have changed and demands an Abschlag payment of 214,00 € to a new IBAN by 11.09.2026, threatening to cut off electricity without further notice if payment is not received. The new IBAN fails checksum validation and the account holder name and contact instructions match typical phishing/scam patterns, so this should be treated with strong suspicion.
data.explanation: This letter looks like it could be a scam trying to trick you into sending money to a fraudulent account by impersonating your energy provider. Genuine utilities rarely change bank details this way, and the IBAN given does not pass a basic validity check. Do not transfer any money or call the phone number in the letter. Instead, contact Stadtwerke Musterstadt using the phone number or address from a previous genuine bill, or their official website, to ask whether this letter is real. If you already paid, contact your bank immediately to try to recall the transfer and consider reporting it to the police (Polizei) as fraud (Betrug).
